breakfast.name: Tapai (Fermented Cassava)
instructions: Top with coconut milk and sugar
breakfast.description: Mildly sweet fermented cassava — traditional Timorese breakfast.

breakfast.name: Katupa (Rice Cakes)
instructions: Boil 60 min until rice is compact
breakfast.description: Compressed rice cakes wrapped in coconut leaves.

breakfast.name: Katupa (Rice in Woven Palm Leaf)
instructions: Weave coconut leaves into small diamond-shaped pouches — this is the art
Fill each pouch about half with rice — it swells as it cooks
Boil pouches in salted coconut milk-water for 1 hour
The rice compresses inside the leaf, becoming a dense, fragrant cake
Unwrap the leaf — the rice has a diamond pattern imprinted from the weaving
Serve with any stew or curry, or just with sambal
The weaving technique is passed down through generations — it takes practice to learn the fold
breakfast.description: Rice cooked inside woven coconut leaf pouches — the leaves imprint a diamond pattern onto the compressed rice. The intricate weaving technique has gone viral as an example of Southeast Asian edible craft. A festive food in East Timor, especially for celebrations and ceremonies.

lunch.name: Ikan Pepes (Spiced Fish in Banana Leaf)
lunch.description: Fish steamed in banana leaf with aromatic spice paste.

lunch.name: Batar Da'an (Corn and Mung Bean Stew)
instructions: Add coconut milk, simmer until thick
lunch.description: Thick corn and bean stew — a Timorese staple.

lunch.name: Batar Da'an (Corn and Mung Bean Stew)
instructions: Boil soaked corn until starting to soften — 30 min
Add pumpkin cubes and coconut milk
Simmer until everything is tender and the stew thickens
Add greens in the last 5 minutes
This is Timor-Leste's staple — corn, not rice, is the traditional grain
The thick, hearty consistency makes it both a soup and a main course
lunch.description: East Timor's traditional staple — corn and mung beans simmered with pumpkin and coconut milk into a thick, nourishing stew. Corn, not rice, is the ancestral grain of Timor-Leste. The hearty simplicity and the beautiful golden color from the pumpkin have earned attention from food travel creators.

dinner.name: Tukir (Braised Pork)
dinner.description: Slow-braised pork with tamarind and turmeric.

dinner.name: Ikan Saboko (Grilled Fish with Sambal)
ingredients: 4 whole fresh fish (snapper, mackerel, or tuna)
Sambal: red chilies, garlic, shallots, lime juice, salt
instructions: Make sambal: pound chilies, garlic, shallots, add lime juice and salt
Grill over charcoal until leaves are charred and fish is cooked through — 10-15 min
Unwrap at the table — the banana leaf steams the fish while the charcoal smokes it
Serve with rice, extra sambal, and lime
The beach-side grilling scene in Dili is the viral image of Timorese food
dinner.description: Fresh fish stuffed with chili sambal, wrapped in banana leaves, and grilled over beach-side charcoal — East Timor's coastal cooking at its purest. The banana-leaf unwrap reveal and the beachside setting have made Dili's grilled fish a viral food-travel destination scene.

snacks.name: Pastel de Nata Timorense (Timorese Egg Tart)
ingredients: Filling: egg yolks, sugar, coconut milk (Timorese twist), vanilla, cinnamon
Powdered sugar and cinnamon for dusting
instructions: Line muffin tins with puff pastry
Make custard: whisk yolks, sugar, coconut milk, vanilla
Pour into pastry shells — don't overfill
Bake at 220°C until pastry is crispy and custard has charred spots on top
Dust with cinnamon and powdered sugar
The Portuguese legacy meets tropical coconut — East Timor's colonial fusion in a pastry
The charred custard spots are the sign of a proper pastel
snacks.description: East Timor's take on the Portuguese egg tart — with coconut milk replacing regular milk, a tropical twist on the Lisbon classic. Portugal's colonial legacy lives on in Dili's bakeries. The coconut-custard version has gained attention as a unique fusion in the global pastel de nata trend.

desserts.name: Bibinka (Coconut Cake)
instructions: Mix rice flour, coconut milk, sugar, eggs

desserts.name: Bibinka (Coconut Rice Cake)
instructions: Mix rice flour, coconut milk, sugar, eggs into a smooth batter
Line baking pan with banana leaves
Bake at 175°C for 35-40 min until set and golden on top
The banana leaf infuses a subtle green, grassy flavor
Cut into squares and serve warm or at room temperature
A celebratory cake found across Southeast Asia but with Timorese variations
desserts.description: A coconut-milk rice cake baked on banana leaves — East Timor's version of a dessert found across Southeast Asia and the Pacific. The banana leaf lining gives it a subtle grassy aroma that elevates the simple coconut-rice base. A staple of Timorese celebrations.

drinks.name: Ai-Café (Timorese Coffee)
drinks.description: Strong, rich Timorese coffee — world-renowned single origin.
